title: Verification cell registry
description: Machine-readable registry of audit cells. A cell is a failure class crossed with entry-point classes and failure modes. Lessons live as detector fixtures, not as objects of audit. Statuses reuse the evidence-first ladder: proven, model-checked, tested, static-refinement, reviewed, open.

project.description: Name of the project or product configuration the registry describes.

generated.description: Date the registry was last regenerated by hand or tooling.

taxonomy.description: The bounded taxonomy the cells belong to. A cell that fits no class is an unroutable finding, not a new cell.

version.description: Taxonomy version. Changing classes is a reviewed change, not an edit.

classes.description: Failure classes in scope, e.g. security, correctness, maintainability, performance.

coverage_status.description: Strongest honest label the evidence supports. open means the cell exists but no detector has exercised it. A non-open cell must name at least one detector.

id.description: Stable detector ID, referenced by lessons and evidence.

kind.description: Channel of the detector. A test detector needs an artifact or a reproducing command.

artifact.description: Path to the detector artifact relative to the project root, or a URL.

command.description: Command that reproduces the detector result.

mutation_fixture.description: Fixture or mutation that must make this detector fail. A detector without one has not been verified.

mutation_exemption.description: Why no repository source mutation can falsify this detector (platform semantics, a configuration control, or a core-engine property). A documented exemption is reported as info by CL2 instead of an unverified warning.

last_verified.description: When the detector was last exercised. Stale detector evidence is a finding.

title.description: Falsifiable statement of the failure class this cell covers.

failure_class.description: Narrower failure class, e.g. broken-access-control or check-then-act.

entry_points.description: Paths that must be covered, e.g. http, batch, import, admin, migration, recovery, background-job.

failure_mode.description: Required behavior when the cell is exercised: refuse, abort, roll back, degrade safely, or detect and report.

detectors.description: Detectors that exercise this cell. Required and non-empty for any non-open coverage status.

claim_ids.description: Claim-ledger IDs this cell provides evidence for.

residual_risk.description: What remains unproven even when all detectors pass.

limitations.description: Known limits and next evidence needed. Required when coverage_status is open.

owner.description: Person or role accountable for the cell. 'unassigned' is allowed but visible.

last_seen.description: When the cell was last exercised or reviewed.
